definitions.explanation: An expression of unwillingness or opposition, typically shown indirectly through facial expression or attitude rather than outright refusal. Almost always used in the fixed phrase {難色|なんしょく}を{示|しめ}す.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{難色|なんしょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}した→示す：01948_shimesu⟧。
⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{価格|かかく}→価格：00147_kakaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{難色|なんしょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}している→示す：01948_shimesu⟧。
examples.english: The other party is showing displeasure with the price.

examples.japanese: ⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{提案|ていあん}した→提案する：06057_teiansuru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{住民|じゅうみん}→住民：03281_juumin⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{難色|なんしょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}され→示す：01948_shimesu⟧、⟦{見直|みなお}し→見直し：09340_minaoshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迫|せま}られた→迫る：03928_semaru⟧。
examples.english: We proposed the plan, but residents expressed their disapproval, and we were forced to reconsider.

notes:
USAGE:
{難色|なんしょく} is almost exclusively used in the set phrase {難色|なんしょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}す→示す：01948_shimesu⟧ (to show reluctance/disapproval). Literally "difficult color" — referring to an unhappy facial expression. It conveys indirect opposition rather than outright refusal, fitting the Japanese cultural pattern of expressing disagreement obliquely.
This word is rarely used outside the {難色|なんしょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}す→示す：01948_shimesu⟧ pattern. It appears frequently in news and business contexts to describe someone who is not directly refusing but is clearly not happy about a proposal.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {難色|なんしょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}す→示す：01948_shimesu⟧ (to show reluctance/disapproval — the standard expression)
- ～⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{難色|なんしょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}す→示す：01948_shimesu⟧ (to show reluctance toward ~)
